extracted.intended_audience: journal editors (especially those new to editing or to specific research-ethics topics)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and training modules for journal editors on handling research-ethics issues in submitted manuscripts (ethics approvals, informed consent, animal ethics, internet research, trial registration) and related editorial responsibilities (peer review, plagiarism, code of conduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Approval (human studies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the ethics approval requirements for human studies in the life sciences and social sciences journals, or any journals that publish articles affecting public health or human welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 gives an overview of ethics approval requirements and aims to demystify requirements and explain the practical aspects of handling manuscripts that involve human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent (participation and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for informed consent to participate in research and informed consent for publication of individual data and images, covering life and social sciences and newer fields in the hard sciences that are using individuals for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 discusses both consent to participate and consent for publication of individually identifiable data/images and addresses where these consents are required and how editors should handle related manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of ethics requirements for animal studies and when ethics approval is required in all fields that use animal subjects, including life sciences and disciplines that may only rarely use these methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 3 explains when ethics approval is necessary for animal work and provides practical guidance for editors on handling manuscripts reporting animal research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics of Internet Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics and consent requirements for internet research studies and the specific associated challenges for studies using online data or interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 4 considers the special issues raised by internet research (across life and social sciences and some hard-science uses of the internet) and aims to clarify consent and ethical expectations for editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for clinical trial registration for life sciences journals, or any journals that publish articles affecting public health or human welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 5 presents trial registration requirements and practical aspects editors should check for manuscripts reporting clinical trials (e.g., registry entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Editors' Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal Editors' Code of Conduct sets out the standards and expectations associated with the role of Editor-in-Chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated course provides an overview of the Code so editors understand their responsibilities and conduct expectations; listed under Editor Resources as linked training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality is a fundamental aspect of the peer review process that editors must uphold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Fundamentals of Peer Review' course outlines confidentiality (and conflicts of interest) as a basic editorial responsibility when managing peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (peer review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and management of conflicts of interest in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer-review fundamentals module explains how to recognise conflicts of interest among reviewers and authors and the expectations for handling them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of a good reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes and behaviours that constitute a strong peer reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fundamentals of Peer Review course explains how to identify the characteristics of a good reviewer to inform reviewer selection and evaluation of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for inviting reviewers to assess manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer-review course covers how to invite reviewers effectively, including considerations for selection, invitation wording, and assessing suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: How editors should assess the quality and usefulness of peer review reports received for a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course explains how to evaluate reviewer reports to inform editorial decisions; included under 'Fundamentals of Peer Review.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism: detection, assessment, and action
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding different types of plagiarism, practicalities of using Crossref Similarity Check, and how to assess and take action on any text overlap detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated plagiarism course teaches editors how to interpret similarity reports, distinguish acceptable overlap from problematic text reuse, and follow up with appropriate editorial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRR (iThenticate Report & Response) service usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional tool (IRR) provided by Springer Nature that analyses the Crossref Similarity Report and provides editors with a recommendation for new submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors can use the IRR service to get an analysis and recommendation regarding text similarity for submitted manuscripts as part of handling potential plagiarism or overlap.
